retained_skill: Infer and implement the variable-length binary record layout, including field widths, byte order, cursor advancement, and CSV conversion.
bottleneck: All 12 scored attempts reached binary inspection, but the date field is only an integer day offset and the required epoch is absent from the task. Near-successes therefore guessed plausible epochs; five attempts also exhausted time while repeatedly reinterpreting bytes.
change: Instruction repair only: state the missing date epoch. This leaves the binary-layout inference entirely with the student and lets it convert a correctly decoded day offset instead of guessing an unobservable convention. No separate simplification is added because fewer than half of attempts ended at a limit and the defect affected near-complete attempts.
restore: Remove the standalone sentence identifying the date epoch to restore the original task; no environment, fixture, solution, or verifier behavior changes.
prediction: Attempts that already infer the cursor-based record layout will stop guessing Unix-, 2000-, 2001-, or 2024-based dates and instead apply the stated epoch. This is refuted if replaying attempt 08 with only that date conversion changed still fails any verifier check, or if the next group continues to produce otherwise-correct CSVs with wrong dates.
